forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For integer parameters a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if the floor inequality holds for every positive integer d, then each explicitly defined exponent e_d is nonnegative for every d between 1 and r+b, and the ratio of q-Pochhammer symbols R_{a,b,r}(q) factors as a finite product of cyclotomic polynomials Phi_d(q) with those exponents. Therefore R_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial with integer coefficients.
quantifier_order: Choose integers a, b, r satisfying 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
Assume that for every positive integer d, the stated floor inequality holds.
For every integer d with 1 <= d <= r+b, define e_d by the given floor formula.
For every such d, conclude that e_d is nonnegative.
Conclude that R_{a,b,r}(q) equals the finite product over d from 1 to r+b of cyclotomic polynomials Phi_d(q) raised to e_d, and hence lies in the integer polynomial ring in q.

payload.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, and set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b). Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then for every integer d with 1 <= d <= r+b, the integer e_d := floor((r+b)/d) + floor(a/d) - floor((r+a)/d) - floor(b/d) is nonnegative, and one has the cyclotomic factorization R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d=1}^{r+b} Phi_d(q)^(e_d), where Phi_d(q) is the d-th cyclotomic polynomial. In particular, R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q].

result_payload.proof_nl:
Set e_d := floor((r+b)/d) + floor(a/d) - floor((r+a)/d) - floor(b/d). The hypothesis says that for every positive integer d,
floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d).
Rearranging gives
 e_d = [floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d)] - [floor(b/d) - floor(a/d)] >= 0.
Thus e_d is a nonnegative integer for every positive d, and in particular for every d with 1 <= d <= r+b.

Now rewrite R_{a,b,r}(q). From the definition (q;q)_n = product_{j=1}^n (1-q^j), we have
 (q;q)_{r+b}/(q;q)_{r+a} = product_{m=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1-q^m),
while
 (q;q)_a/(q;q)_b = 1 / product_{j=a+1}^{b} (1-q^j).
Therefore
 R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{j=a+1}^{b} ((1-q^{r+j})/(1-q^j)),
with the usual empty-product value 1 when a=b.

For each integer m >= 1, use the standard cyclotomic factorization
 q^m - 1 = product_{d|m} Phi_d(q).
Then
 1 - q^m = -(q^m - 1) = - product_{d|m} Phi_d(q).
Hence for each j,
 (1-q^{r+j})/(1-q^j)
 = [ - product_{d|(r+j)} Phi_d(q) ] / [ - product_{d|j} Phi_d(q) ]
 = product_{d|(r+j)} Phi_d(q) * product_{d|j} Phi_d(q)^(-1).
Multiplying these identities over j = a+1, ..., b and collecting equal cyclotomic factors, the exponent of Phi_d(q) in the total product is
 c_d := #{j : a < j <= b, d | (r+j)} - #{j : a < j <= b, d | j}.

The first count is the number of multiples of d in the interval [r+a+1, r+b], so
 #{j : a < j <= b, d | (r+j)} = floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d).
The second count is the number of multiples of d in [a+1, b], so
 #{j : a < j <= b, d | j} = floor(b/d) - floor(a/d).
Therefore
 c_d = floor((r+b)/d) + floor(a/d) - floor((r+a)/d) - floor(b/d) = e_d.

If d > r+b, then both counts are 0, because every integer occurring in the two intervals is at most r+b. Hence c_d = 0 for d > r+b. Thus the factorization is finite and equals
 R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d=1}^{r+b} Phi_d(q)^(e_d).
This is exactly the asserted cyclotomic factorization.

Finally, each e_d is a nonnegative integer, and each cyclotomic polynomial Phi_d(q) lies in Z[q]. Therefore the finite product product_{d=1}^{r+b} Phi_d(q)^(e_d) belongs to Z[q]. Hence R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q].
result_payload.proof_summary: Rearrange the assumed floor inequality to obtain e_d >= 0. Then rewrite the q-Pochhammer ratio as product_{j=a+1}^b (1-q^{r+j})/(1-q^j), factor each 1-q^m via cyclotomic polynomials, and count multiples of d in the relevant intervals; the resulting exponent is exactly e_d, giving the finite cyclotomic factorization and therefore R_{a,b,r}(q) in Z[q].

used_external_facts: Standard cyclotomic factorization q^m - 1 = product_{d|m} Phi_d(q).
Each cyclotomic polynomial Phi_d(q) has integer coefficients, i.e. Phi_d(q) is in Z[q].
